parsed.rationale: Deploying mfa:admin and mfa:dbadmin together makes exfiltration impossible, and no single control does. Why the pair works: (1) foothold_dc and foothold_adfs can only come from auth_dc and auth_adfs, which both require NOT mfa_admin. So mfa:admin means admin_dc and admin_adfs can never be reached. (2) auth_db, auth_fileserver and auth_backup each require (NOT mfa_dbadmin OR admin_dc OR admin_adfs). With mfa:dbadmin deployed and admin_dc/admin_adfs unreachable, the attacker can never get a foothold on db, fileserver or backup. (3) Every exfiltrate technique needs admin on one of those three hosts, so exfiltration cannot happen. Why no single control works: phishing is always available, giving foothold_workstation and stolen_user. Checking each relevant control alone: (a) segmented: the attacker escalates the workstation (not patched), pivots internally, authenticates to ciserver (mfa:user is bypassed by the workstation foothold), kerberoasts to get stolen_admin, escalates ciserver, leaks stolen_dbadmin, then authenticates to db, escalates and exfiltrates. (b) mfa:admin: the same ciserver path yields stolen_dbadmin, and auth_db succeeds because mfa:dbadmin is absent. (c) mfa:dbadmin: auth_dc succeeds with stolen_admin, then admin_dc, which bypasses mfa:dbadmin on db. (d) Any patch alone: patching appserver, apiserver or ciserver is bypassed by stolen_admin; patching workstation or laptop does nothing without segmentation; patching db, fileserver or backup leaves the other two targets open; patching web, proxy, vpn, dc or adfs blocks nothing essential. (e) mfa:user: bypassed by the phished workstation foothold.
